attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Reject the entry as merely restating P != NP.
attacks.method: Check whether the statement is logically stronger and supplies a distinct nonuniform target rather than an algorithmic reformulation.
attacks.notes: It is a direct target, not a mechanism; it remains useful only as the root node for more specific descendants.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use natural proofs to rule out all possible approaches.
attacks.method: Separate a barrier against a broad proof technique from a contradiction to the existential lower-bound statement.
attacks.notes: Natural-proofs results constrain methods but do not refute the target.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that SAT witnesses certify positive errors but no polynomial certificate is available for negative errors.
attacks.method: Audit whether the statement silently assumes NP = coNP for its UNSAT certificates.
attacks.notes: The certificate obligation is the central unresolved gate and prevents the entry from being a completed diagonalization.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Construct a circuit that memorizes the polynomial anti-checker list.
attacks.method: Charge the circuit for recognizing the exact produced formulas and check whether memorization stays within n^k.
attacks.notes: A polynomial list can be memorized by some circuits, but the quantifier requires defeating every size n^k circuit; a valid construction must diagonalize after accounting for this.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that proving the witnessing formulas tautological already assumes SAT circuit lower bounds.
attacks.method: Inspect the definition and isolate which f-properties can be proved independently of the target lower bound.
attacks.notes: The cited framework supplies the implication, but a noncircular explicit f remains the main obstacle.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Argue that an Extended Frege lower bound need not survive adding witnessing axioms.
attacks.method: Compare the exact augmented proof system with ordinary EF and reject any unsupported transfer.
attacks.notes: The hypothesis explicitly targets the augmented system, so failure of transfer from ordinary EF is not a contradiction.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Reject the conjecture because it embeds an unproved circuit-hardness premise.
attacks.method: Separate the generator-hardness implication from the independent task of proving hardness for f.
attacks.notes: The route is conditional until the function hardness is established, but the exact bridge remains unresolved.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Find b values accidentally lying in the generator range, making the formulas non-tautological.
attacks.method: Require explicit b outside the range and audit whether such b can be selected without solving range avoidance.
attacks.notes: Selecting certified missing outputs is itself a substantive gate, not a refutation of the existential statement.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: For a fixed g, define the complement of its range and try to show it contains an infinite NP subset.
attacks.method: Audit the complexity of certifying non-membership in Range(g).
attacks.notes: The complement is in coNP in general, not automatically NP, so the diagonal set is not an immediate counterexample.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Assume an optimal proof system and derive failure of the generator.
attacks.method: Check whether optimality yields a polynomially bounded system or only simulation optimality.
attacks.notes: An optimal proof system need not be polynomially bounded; the conjecture is not directly contradicted.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Construct pairs whose equivalence itself is hard to establish, making explicitness circular.
attacks.method: Require a direct polynomial-time proof of semantic equivalence independent of EF.
attacks.notes: Candidate pairs must have transparent equivalence; this narrows but does not destroy the route.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use intermediate circuits with globally different structure to bypass any local invariant.
attacks.method: Audit whether the approximately relation permits such shortcuts through deletion and seven-gate additions.
attacks.notes: No universal shortcut theorem or preserved lower-bound invariant is currently established.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that canonical-pair definitions vary and the statement is encoding dependent.
attacks.method: Fix a standard polynomially equivalent encoding and verify invariance under reductions.
attacks.notes: Polynomially equivalent canonical encodings preserve P-separability.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use proof-length thresholds to build a separator.
attacks.method: Check whether deciding which side has a short proof is itself polynomial-time.
attacks.notes: Membership has NP witnesses but no known deterministic separator.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Apply known extraction only to roABP, formula, or multilinear IPS.
attacks.method: Compare every hypothesis quantifier with existing fragment-specific theorems.
attacks.notes: Known results do not cover unrestricted full IPS, which is exactly the missing transfer.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Observe that an explicit superpolynomial lower bound for general algebraic circuits is itself open.
attacks.method: Separate the extraction lemma from the hard-polynomial theorem.
attacks.notes: The route contains two major gates; either would still be independently valuable.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Reject the entry as a restatement of an existing qualitative dichotomy.
attacks.method: Compare the added constructive extraction and explicit uniformity requirements with the cited theorem.
attacks.notes: The novelty claim is unassessed; value lies in making the lower-bound object explicit and machine-checkable.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: If no polynomial-size depth-d PIT circuits exist, neither stated branch applies.
attacks.method: Add the absence of such circuits as an algebraic circuit lower-bound outcome.
attacks.notes: Nonexistence is itself a lower bound and can be treated as a third successful outcome.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Point out that the resulting lower-bound disjunction does not by itself prove P != NP.
attacks.method: Record the exact downstream implications without inflating them.
attacks.notes: It is a barrier-breaking lemma rather than a direct resolution.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use known lower bounds against restricted black-box PIT constructions.
attacks.method: Check whether they apply to arbitrary white-box deterministic algorithms.
attacks.notes: Black-box limitations do not refute general deterministic PIT.
